hero.title: Experimental media systems spanning film, sound, computation, installation, and speculative fiction.
hero.lede: Tony Yanick is an artist, educator, and computational media researcher working across film/video, sound, installation, generative systems, and participatory media environments. His work investigates how technological infrastructures, speculative narratives, and audiovisual systems shape perception, collective desire, and lived experience through unstable relationships between image, signal, memory, and space.

works.title: Works as environments to enter, activate, and never fully resolve.

statement.title: My work operates through fiction—not as representation, but as a force that produces conditions.
paragraphs: I am interested in how narrative, myth, mediated images, and technological systems organize collective desire, and how these structures persist, circulate, and mutate across media environments.

The work develops across film, sound, installation, performance, and computational media—not as movement between disciplines, but as interference between forms. Image, sound, code, archives, and spatial systems interact to produce unstable relationships between perception, atmosphere, participation, and interpretation.

Many works unfold through projected image, live signal routing, synthetic voice, tape-based processes, generative image systems, networked participation, or computational feedback structures. Installations are treated less as static objects than as evolving conditions in which viewers encounter fragments, delays, repetitions, and unstable narrative relations over time.

I return repeatedly to temporal displacement. Fragments of possible worlds appear out of sequence—past events reconfigured as future projections, speculative structures embedded within existing archives, signals that arrive too early or too late.
Computational systems extend this condition. I engage generative and networked media not simply as tools for production, but as infrastructures that compress, redistribute, and reorganize perception.
There is no stable image at the end of this process—only signals that continue to circulate.

research.title: Investigating computational media as operational environments rather than neutral tools.

cards.title: Limits of CTRL
cards.text: Limits of CTRL: Neural Bending and the Generic Machine investigates generative AI models as infrastructural cultural systems rather than image-generation tools. The research focuses on intervention, probabilistic behavior, recursion, operational constraints, and the relationship between synthetic media and collective perception.

cards.title: Neural bending
cards.text: Neural bending treats generative systems as mutable environments whose internal operations can be redirected through interference, recursion, constraint, feedback, and distributed procedural modification rather than prompt-based output extraction alone.

cards.title: Media environments
cards.text: The research examines how computational media reorganizes spectatorship, memory, labor, authorship, and perception through interfaces, datasets, network structures, synthetic imagery, and algorithmic distribution systems.

teaching.title: Teaching across systems rather than fixed disciplines.
teaching.intro: Courses combine moving image production, sound design, editing, installation practice, computational media, experimental publishing, and critical media theory through project-based collaborative learning environments. Students are encouraged to move fluidly between analog and digital processes while developing technical literacy, conceptual rigor, and sustainable creative workflows.

materials.title: Systems-based media studio
materials.text: A studio model that asks students to build relationships between image, sound, code, archive, installation, and spatial experience rather than treating media as separate disciplines.

materials.title: Computational media as environment
materials.text: Assignments introduce computational systems as cultural and perceptual infrastructures, foregrounding constraints, feedback, iteration, recursion, and critical technical literacy through hands-on experimentation.

materials.title: Analog / digital publication systems
materials.text: A hybrid print and screen sequence connecting risograph processes, archives, typography, sequencing, networked distribution, and experimental publishing workflows.

projects.title: HYPNAGNOSIS
projects.format: Risograph works, altered-state artifacts, print/media environment
projects.summary: Artifacts of altered states: risograph works and media structures concerned with sleep paralysis, liminal perception, unstable embodiment, dream architectures, and psychological thresholds.
projects.system: The project treats the printed artifact as a perceptual interface: color separation, repetition, grain, and registration drift become evidence of an unstable body moving between waking and dream states.
projects.embed: Image sequence / print documentation embed slot

projects.title: COSMOMORPHOSIS
projects.format: Generative audiovisual installation driven by ISS telemetry
projects.summary: A generative audiovisual installation in which ISS telemetry modulates image, sound, duration, and nonlinear temporal behavior.
projects.system: Orbital data functions as more than input; it becomes an environmental condition that produces evolving audiovisual drift, delayed perception, and a sense of scale between body, signal, and planetary infrastructure.
projects.embed: Video / live data capture embed slot

projects.title: TRANSMISSIONS
projects.format: Speculative transmission system, sound, voice, distributed media
projects.summary: A speculative transmission system mixing hip-hop, spoken word, science fiction, pirate radio aesthetics, distributed signal structures, and broken broadcast environments.
projects.system: TRANSMISSIONS frames broadcast as a fractured commons: voice, rhythm, and signal circulate through unstable infrastructures where participation changes the conditions of reception.
projects.embed: Audio player / transmission archive embed slot

projects.title: SHAPE OF A PACKET
projects.summary: A networked participatory installation involving mobile systems, local connectivity, archives, participant contribution, and distributed media.
projects.system: The work makes network behavior perceptible as social and spatial form: packets, contributions, and local archives become a temporary media environment assembled by participants.
projects.embed: Local network interface / documentation embed slot

projects.title: N2: THE SECRETARY
projects.format: Language, signal, archive, synthetic image/sound system
projects.summary: A layered configuration of language, signal, sound, and image in which archives and synthetic media operate as unstable evidence.
projects.system: Documents, recordings, and generated images are organized as a speculative administrative system whose authority remains unresolved.

projects.title: ARTIFICIAL CINEMA
projects.summary: A computational audiovisual environment treating AI and media systems as operative environments rather than output generators.
projects.system: The project approaches model behavior as cinematic condition: perception is reorganized through prompts, constraints, recursive feedback, generated fragments, and temporal arrangement.
projects.embed: A/V excerpt / computational system capture embed slot

projects.title: VARIATION 79 / PODKOP
projects.summary: Experimental audiovisual works concerned with repetition, recursion, mediated memory, and the residues of speculative systems.
projects.system: These works extend a recurring concern with temporal displacement: fragments return as altered signals, producing a field of repetition, delay, and unresolved evidence.
projects.embed: Video excerpt / screening documentation embed slot

projects.title: The Fixers: Naudia Loftis
projects.summary: A collaborative documentary centered on a seventeen-year-old community organizer in Cleveland’s Kinsman neighborhood.
projects.system: Structured through interviews with friends and family, the film foregrounds lived experience within conditions shaped by systemic violence and social instability. Rather than imposing an external narrative, the work creates space for participants to articulate their perspectives through dialogue, proximity, and trust.
projects.embed: Documentary excerpt / screening documentation embed slot

projects.title: Make America Great Again ... And Again
projects.summary: An experimental video work and Short and Sweet Festival Outstanding Film award winner drawing on Octavia E. Butler’s Parable trilogy.
projects.system: The project examines political language as a mechanism of narrative construction and control, exploring the relationship between speculative fiction and contemporary political reality. Through montage, abstraction, and layered imagery, it asks not what greatness is, but for whom it is constructed and at what cost.
projects.embed: Experimental video excerpt / screening documentation embed slot

projects.title: surFACE
projects.format: Short film, analog recording systems, tape-based process
projects.summary: A short film produced as part of the larger TAPEHEADS project, investigating analog recording systems, tape-based processes, and the material conditions of image and sound.
projects.system: Built from a repetitive drawing practice centered on abstracted faces, the film treats marks as raw material within recording, layering, playback, and transformation. The screen becomes an apparatus where image and sound co-evolve through repetition, distortion, and feedback.
projects.embed: Short film excerpt / analog feedback documentation embed slot

projects.title: Flow Lines (3-channel video)
projects.summary: A collaborative video work developed in response to Isaac Julien’s Kapital, exploring the movement of value through geography, history, and narrative.
projects.system: Centered on the Niagara River as both physical flow and historical boundary connected to the Underground Railroad, the piece layers landscape, memory, and migration through image, rhythm, and poetic language. It approaches landscape as a living system through which histories are carried, transformed, and reinterpreted.
projects.embed: Three-channel video excerpt / installation documentation embed slot

projects.title: BOBBI LYNN
projects.summary: A music video that explores memory and familial relationships through generative image systems.
projects.system: Centered on a son’s recollection of his relationship with his mother, the work replaces photographic reconstruction with synthetic image generation. Drawing on Roland Barthes’ distinction between studium and punctum, it examines how memory, identity, intimacy, and representation become mediated through machine-generated imagery.
projects.embed: Music video excerpt / generative image documentation embed slot

projects.title: Dossier 37
projects.format: Audiovisual work, forensic interface, data visualization
projects.summary: An audiovisual work developed in collaboration with AUDINT that investigates the unstable territory between sonic warfare, disinformation, and state narrative production.
projects.system: Emerging from discourse surrounding alleged sonic attacks on US diplomatic personnel in Cuba and South China, the project examines how fear, rumor, and geopolitical speculation circulate through media systems as forms of perceptual instability. Structured as a forensic and speculative timeline, it visualizes Twitter activity and signal environments around Havana Syndrome.
